evidence.quote: A TIG welder was utilized to produce a DED-Arc alloy with dimensions of 150 mm × 15 mm × 95 mm. A piece of GW93K alloy with a thickness of 20 mm was used as a substrate. Ar gas was employed as a protective atmosphere to prevent oxidation of the molten alloy.

evidence.quote: residual dislocations in the T6-treated DED-Arc alloy
accumulation of dislocations at GBs
The dislocation accumulation at GBs of cast alloy leads to a significant widening of the GBP zone and PFZ
More uniformly distributed dislocations of DED-Arc alloy lead to the formation of more dynamic precipitates in GI.
Fewer twins in the DED-Arc alloys lead to a more uniform stress distribution.
These characteristics promote the initiation of cracks at the GBs, ultimately resulting in more significant intergranular fractures in the cast alloy

mechanisms.name: dislocation-grain boundary competition for solute segregation

evidence.quote: The competition between dislocations and GBs for the segregation of RE atoms is analyzed with MD simulations and TEM observation. It is found that the dislocations in DED-Arc alloys significantly reduce the element segregation to GBs.

The dislocation accumulation at GBs of cast alloy leads to a significant widening of the GBP zone and PFZ, which will hinder the transfer of stress along the grains, leading to further accumulation of stress at the GBs.
